walkthroughs.h2: Why did the wartime alliance break down?
walkthroughs.body_html: Ideological hostility between liberal capitalism and communism resumed after 1945. Disagreements emerged at Potsdam over reparations and free elections in Eastern Europe. Stalin imposed friendly regimes by 1948 (the Prague coup in February). Churchill's 1946 Fulton 'Iron Curtain' speech and Kennan's 1946 Long Telegram framed Soviet expansionism. Mutual suspicion hardened into structural rivalry.

Faced with Greek and Turkish crises in 1947, Truman articulated containment on 12 March, pledging USD 400 million in aid. Marshall's 5 June Harvard speech offered economic assistance to all Europe; Soviets refused. The Cominform was created in September 1947 and Comecon in 1949. By 1949 NATO codified Western alliance; the Federal Republic of Germany was established in May 1949, the GDR in October.

Orthodox historians (Schlesinger) blamed Stalin's expansionism. Revisionists (William Appleman Williams) emphasised US economic imperatives. Post-revisionists (John Lewis Gaddis) cited structural factors and miscommunication; with the post-1991 archives, Gaddis returned to Stalin-centred explanations, arguing his ideological certainty and security paranoia made Cold War unavoidable.

options: Stalin rejected the Marshall Plan because it required countries to fight Germany again.

options: He saw it as dollar imperialism that would pull Eastern Europe into the US orbit; he set up Comecon as an Eastern bloc alternative and blocked satellite states from joining.
Stalin rejected the Marshall Plan because the USSR did not need money after WWII.
